yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact survives: dates, offices, Saturday hours, $10, the $2.50 fee, tag sizes (with helpful metric), the free permit for the school year, and the thinning rationale. "Year 4 kids" sensibly localises fourth graders.
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "people who can't cut their own tree get first dibs", "just pop in the pass or voucher number", "heads up: the $2.50 service fee still applies", "does the bush a good turn".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural, plain-spoken Australian; the one tic is the repeated "Chrissie tree", which Australians say but not eight times in a notice.
yarn-dinkum.register: A light, friendly layer right for level 2: "first dibs", "heads up", "have a proper read"; no swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the informative, helpful tone of a public notice, just friendlier: "Get in touch with us for current opening hours."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads smoothly: "Buy one online through recreation.gov and there's an extra $2.50 service fee on top."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied apart from the leaned-on "Chrissie tree".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All the facts survive, with added advice and comment that the notice doesn't give: "so have your password handy", "so don't go changing your mind", "which is only fair", "Everyone's a winner." "Can't swing an axe? No worries." broadens the priority group a little.
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly exact: "hand over any dosh", "Give 'em a bell", "they'll sting you an extra $2.50", "Now, the damage." all fit.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural, but the opener and closer are stock: "Here's one for ya." and "Everyone's a winner."; "packed in like sardines" is a cliché.
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 2: a promo-yarn voice with tags and asides throughout, "wouldn't ya know it", "mind", "'em"; no swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: The neutral notice turns into a chatty sales pitch: "And here's a good one for the families"; the information stays clear.
yarn-troppo.flow: Lively and readable; a few stacked asides: "Got your eye on something bigger, taller than 10 feet and/or wider than 5 inches? That needs an extra tag."
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range: "dosh", "bell", "sting", "the damage", "first dibs", "slapped on"; "Chrissie tree" repeats.
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the notice, but its plain official character is replaced by a pitch.

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every fact survives, with metric conversions and "Year 4 kids".
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "improves the health of the bush", "provide feed for wildlife", "Year 4 kids".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural but very close to the notice's officialese, so the few local words stand out: "Year 4 kids with an Every Kid Outdoors pass are eligible for a free Chrissie tree permit".
yarn-deadset.register: Lighter than level 2: little beyond "Chrissie", "bush" and "Year 4 kids" in otherwise official prose.
yarn-deadset.tone: The notice's tone, kept: "It's important to read the overview and need-to-know information carefully before buying the permit."
yarn-deadset.flow: Smooth, though "Chrissie tree" repeats and "Year 4 kids ... are eligible" mixes registers.
yarn-deadset.variety: Leans on "Chrissie tree"; little else to vary.

unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "up for grabs", "with first dibs going to people who can't cut their own tree", "crowded stands of skinny trees".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural, plain English with a few local touches, but leaves the US "Fourth graders" and "through December 20".
unharnessed.register: Light for level 2: "up for grabs", "first dibs" and a relaxed register, little else.
unharnessed.tone: The notice's informative tone, kept and made friendly: "Cutting a Christmas tree is good for the health of the forest, too."
unharnessed.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "Taking these trees out of designated areas helps the other trees grow bigger".
unharnessed.variety: Few terms, none leaned on: "up for grabs", "first dibs", "skinny".

engine.sense: The few swaps strain: "Local bush health experts identify areas" turns forest health experts into something like bush medicine, and "improves bush health" reads oddly.
engine.authenticity: Nearly all untouched officialese, with inconsistent swaps: "Chrissy tree permits" at the top and "Chrissie tree" at the end, while the middle keeps "Christmas Tree" and "Fourth graders".
engine.flow: Reads as the original, but the inconsistent spellings jar: "Chrissy tree permits" then "Cutting a Chrissie tree".

summaries.yarn-dinkum: The best: complete, natural, light and friendly, with only the repeated 'Chrissie tree'.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Accurate and lively, but over-cooked for level 2: a sales-yarn voice with added asides.
summaries.yarn-deadset: A faithful light localisation; lighter than asked and leaning on 'Chrissie tree'.
summaries.unharnessed: A smooth, faithful plain-English version with a light Aussie touch, lighter than asked.
summaries.engine: The original with a couple of mechanical swaps, one in the wrong sense.
